mnemonic: Learning 学 with a wall drawn the whole way round it 園, grounds and all, which is more than a school building. Hers is out in the suburbs: がくえん.
notes: 学校 がっこう is the ordinary word for a school. 学園 is grander, a campus with grounds, and it turns up in the names of private ones.
sentence: 彼女は郊外の学園に通っているね。
sentence_meaning: She goes to a school in the suburbs.

mnemonic: The heart 忄 has caught something about the man that will not add up, and nobody in the room can say which part: あやしい.
notes: おかしい is odd in a way that might yet turn out funny. 怪しい puts the weight on the suspicion.
sentence: その男の行動は怪しかったわ。
sentence_meaning: That man's behavior was suspicious.

mnemonic: One mould 型 and a thousand identical shells off the back of it, not one told apart from the next. The camera is the newest of those: かた.
notes: Same reading as 方 かた, the polite word for a person, and 肩 かた, shoulder. This one is the mould, and the model number on the box.
sentence: 新しい型のカメラを買いました。
sentence_meaning: I bought a new-model camera.

mnemonic: Water 氵 doing the only thing water does, and up at the top of the river it does it fast: ながれ.
notes: 流す ながす is you letting something go with it. 流れ is the movement itself, as a noun.
sentence: 川の上流は流れが速いよ。
sentence_meaning: The river flows fast upstream.

mnemonic: What is still on the plate once everybody has stopped eating. The rest of the work is coming home with you: のこり.
notes: 余り あまり is the surplus, what there was more than enough of. 残り is what has not been got through yet.
sentence: 仕事の残りは家でします。
sentence_meaning: I'll do the rest of the work at home.

mnemonic: A person 亻 and somebody they had no arrangement whatever to meet, in one street at one minute. Nobody planned a second of it: ぐうぜん.
notes: 機会 きかい is a chance you could take. 偶然 is a coincidence that simply happened to you.
sentence: 街で偶然友人に会いました。
sentence_meaning: I met a friend by chance downtown.

mnemonic: A tree 木 still young enough to bend right over rather than snap, and the new sofa gives exactly that way when you sit: やわらかい.
sentence: 新しいソファーはとても柔らかいです。
sentence_meaning: The new sofa is really soft.

mnemonic: What comes back through the fingers 触 the moment they land on it. That cloth answers like silk: かんしょく.
notes: 気持ち きもち, 気分 きぶん and 感じ かんじ are how you feel inside. 触る さわる is the act of touching, and 感触 is what comes back through your hand.
sentence: その生地は絹のような感触だ。
sentence_meaning: That cloth feels like silk.

mnemonic: Woman 女 and child 子 pushed together into the word that goes on a register. Eighteen of them in this class: じょし.
notes: 女 おんな and 女性 じょせい are the plain and the formal words, and 女の子 おんなのこ and 少女 しょうじょ are a girl as a person. 女子 is the counting one, for classes, teams and doors.
sentence: このクラスの女子は18人です。
sentence_meaning: There are 18 girls in this class.

mnemonic: The whole lot burnt away 無 with none of it left over. No homework tonight: なし.
sentence: 今日は宿題は無しです。
sentence_meaning: There is no homework today.

mnemonic: Whatever had been standing goes back to a pile of bits and nobody dropped it. The remote simply stopped working: こわれる.
notes: 壊す こわす is you breaking it. 壊れる is it breaking of its own accord.
sentence: テレビのリモコンが壊れてしまいました。
sentence_meaning: The TV remote got broken.

meaning: hard to deal with, weak point
mnemonic: A bitter 苦 taste in the hand 手 you were dealt. Not that you cannot cook, more that you would honestly rather not: にがて.
notes: The reading is irregular, 苦 read にが rather than く.
sentence: 私は料理が苦手です。
sentence_meaning: I'm not good at cooking.

mnemonic: You put the thing through its paces to find out what it actually does, rather than what the box says. He ran the software: ためす.
sentence: 彼はそのソフトウェアを試したの。
sentence_meaning: He tested that software.

mnemonic: He stands 立 apart from the rest of them 派, and the word has nothing to do with looks. A fine man, and everybody says so: りっぱ.
sentence: 彼は立派な人です。
sentence_meaning: He's a fine man.

mnemonic: You take hold of it and turn it, which is the whole difference. A steering wheel does not go round on its own: まわす.
notes: 回る まわる is a thing going round by itself. 回す is you turning it.
sentence: 車のハンドルを回します。
sentence_meaning: I turn the steering wheel of the car.

mnemonic: Nothing happened yesterday and nothing actually hurts, and still your legs weigh twice what they ought to today: なぜか.
notes: 何だか なんだか and どうも do the same job. なぜか keeps the why inside it, since なぜ is why.
sentence: 今日はなぜか体がだるい。
sentence_meaning: I feel sluggish today for some reason.

mnemonic: What you think 意 crossed with what you have actually seen 見, said out loud in a room. I want to hear yours: いけん.
sentence: あなたの意見が聞きたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to hear your opinion.

mnemonic: A big 大 amount 量, both halves saying it flatly and neither exaggerating. What went out on the pavement would not fit the bin: たいりょう.
sentence: 昨日大量のゴミが出たの。
sentence_meaning: A large amount of garbage was put out yesterday.

mnemonic: You carry 提 the plan 案 in and set it down on the table in front of everybody. The idea was his and not yours: ていあん.
sentence: そのアイデアは彼の提案です。
sentence_meaning: That idea is his proposal.

mnemonic: Somebody has to answer 責 for it, and the duty 任 of doing so is a thing you can pick up or leave. He picked it up and resigned: せきにん.
sentence: 彼は失敗の責任を取って、会社を辞めた。
sentence_meaning: He took responsibility for the mistake and resigned from the company.

mnemonic: A hand flat on the lid, keeping the thing down, and the effort of that is the whole word. He said none of what he was thinking: おさえる.
notes: 押す おす is pushing something along. 抑える is pressing down on something so that it cannot come up.
sentence: 彼は怒りを抑えていたの。
sentence_meaning: He was holding back his anger.

meaning: with all of one's strength, at full capacity
mnemonic: The whole 全 of your power 力 with none of it kept back for later. Run, and mean it: ぜんりょく.
sentence: 全力で走れ。
sentence_meaning: Run with all your might!

mnemonic: You take the thing and draw it out longer than it was, and before a run the thing in question is your own legs: のばす.
notes: 伸びる のびる is a thing stretching or growing by itself. 伸ばす is you stretching it.
sentence: ジョギングの前に体を伸ばしましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's stretch before we start jogging.

mnemonic: Somebody under your roof 宀 who does not live there and is not staying the night. That shop is full of young ones: きゃく.
sentence: その店は若い客が多いです。
sentence_meaning: That shop has a lot of young customers.

mnemonic: A king 王 with a country 国 arranged round him, which is the entire definition. Sweden is one, and so are the Netherlands: おうこく.
sentence: スウェーデンやオランダは王国です。
sentence_meaning: Sweden and the Netherlands are kingdoms.

mnemonic: One hand braced 抵 and the other put up against it 抗, and neither of them is giving way. He did not go quietly: ていこう.
sentence: 犯人は警察に抵抗したの。
sentence_meaning: The criminal resisted the police.

mnemonic: Everything stirred 混 through everything else and every thread 乱 pulled a different way at once. The town, after the earthquake: こんらん.
sentence: 地震の後、町は大混乱だったよ。
sentence_meaning: After the earthquake, the town was thrown into chaos.

mnemonic: One clause 条 and then the next matter 件, and the list of them is what you have to meet before anything happens. These are too harsh: じょうけん.
notes: 状態 じょうたい is the state a thing is in. 条件 is the terms attached to it.
sentence: この条件では厳しすぎます。
sentence_meaning: It's too harsh under these conditions.

mnemonic: Rice all over the road 迷 and a heart 惑 that cannot see its way past it, and you are the one who spilled it. Do not do that to people: めいわく.
sentence: 人に迷惑をかけてはいけません。
sentence_meaning: You shouldn't cause trouble for other people.

mnemonic: One person 亻 stood out of the row 列 so that everybody else can see how the thing is done. Look at that one: れい.
sentence: 例を見てください。
sentence_meaning: Please look at the example.

meaning: to rely on, to depend on
mnemonic: You put the whole bundle 束 on somebody else's head 頁 and walk off. Have a go at it yourself first: たよる.
notes: 頼む たのむ is asking somebody for something. 頼る is leaning your weight on them.
sentence: 人に頼らないで、自分でやってごらん。
sentence_meaning: Do it yourself without relying on other people.

mnemonic: A finished 完 ring of jade 璧 without one mark anywhere on the surface of it. His French does not have a seam in it: かんぺき.
notes: 完全 かんぜん is complete, nothing missing. 完璧 is flawless, nothing wrong. The 璧 is jade, not 壁 a wall.
sentence: 彼のフランス語は完璧です。
sentence_meaning: His French is perfect.

mnemonic: One day 日 and then the mark that says do that again 々, and the going on doing it is the entire point: ひび.
notes: 毎日 まいにち is every day as a count. 日々 is the days as they go past, and it leans on the routine of it.
sentence: 日々の努力が大切です。
sentence_meaning: Working hard everyday is crucial.

mnemonic: Something done 行 on purpose 為 rather than something that merely happened. What he did left the room with the wrong idea: こうい.
sentence: 彼の行為はみんなの誤解を招いたわ。
sentence_meaning: His actions ended up misleading everyone.

mnemonic: Whatever else is true and whatever is still unsettled, set the lot aside for a minute. Let us go back and think it through again: ともかく.
notes: とにかく is the same idea with a different vowel and much the same job. せめて and 少なくとも are at least in the sense of a floor, and ようやく and やっと are at last.
sentence: ともかく一度考え直しましょう。
sentence_meaning: At any rate, let's rethink this one more time.

mnemonic: Water going out of the bowl until there is less in it than all 咸 of it was. The population has been at this for years: へる.
notes: 減らす へらす is you reducing something. 減る is it going down on its own.
sentence: 日本では人口が減っています。
sentence_meaning: In Japan, the population is decreasing.

mnemonic: He does not merely put up with it badly, he rearranges his whole morning to avoid it. Rush hour, every single day: きらう.
notes: 嫌い きらい is the adjective, disliking a thing. 嫌う is the verb, actively hating it.
sentence: 父はラッシュアワーを嫌っています。
sentence_meaning: My father hates rush hour.

mnemonic: You know 知 them enough for a nod to fit 合 between you in the street, and not one step further than that: しりあい.
notes: 友達 ともだち and 友人 ゆうじん are friends. 知り合い stops well short of that.
sentence: 街で知り合いを見かけたよ。
sentence_meaning: I saw an acquaintance in town.

mnemonic: The heart 心 in the field 田 and the old man 耂 both working on it at once, which wants a settled room. Wound up, you cannot do it straight: しこう.
notes: 思い おもい is nearer a feeling and 考え かんがえ is a worked-out view. 思考 is the process itself, and it is a formal word.
sentence: 緊張するとまともな思考ができない。
sentence_meaning: You cannot think straight if you are nervous.

mnemonic: You untie 解 the knot first and then decide 決 the thing so that it stays decided. The trouble is finally over: かいけつ.
sentence: トラブルがやっと解決した。
sentence_meaning: The problem has finally been solved.

mnemonic: Cold 冷 and quiet 静 together, which is a temperature rather than a mood. Let us talk about it in that state: れいせい.
notes: 平気 へいき is being unbothered by a thing. 冷静 is keeping your head, and you can manage it while extremely bothered.
sentence: 冷静に話し合いましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's talk calmly.

mnemonic: A person with both arms out and one line drawn straight over the top of them, which is everything above your head: てん.
notes: Same reading as 点 てん, a point or a mark on a test. 空 そら is the sky you look up at. 天 is the heavens, and it is the grander word.
sentence: 天から恵みの雨が降ったね。
sentence_meaning: A blessed rain fell from the heavens.

mnemonic: You did not see it get light and you were sitting there awake the whole time. It happened inside a gap you never noticed: いつのまにか.
sentence: いつの間にか夜が明けていたね。
sentence_meaning: The dawn had broken before we realized it.

meaning: to repair, to cure, to alter
mnemonic: You look at the broken thing dead on 直 and put it back the way it is supposed to be. I did that one myself: なおす.
notes: 直る なおる is a thing mending on its own. 変える かえる turns something into something else, where 直す puts it right.
sentence: 私がそれを直しました。
sentence_meaning: I repaired that.

mnemonic: The same cloth hanging in the same place every day of the year. His posture does not slip once: つねに.
notes: いつも is the everyday always. 常に is formal and firmer with it.
sentence: 彼は常に姿勢がいい。
sentence_meaning: He always has a good attitude.

mnemonic: The person 人 who crossed the line 犯, now kneeling on the far side of it. That is him, over there: はんにん.
sentence: あいつが犯人です。
sentence_meaning: That guy's the culprit.

mnemonic: Somebody says 言 out loud that the thing is allowed 可, and until they have said it, it is not. Ask before you take the day: きょか.
sentence: 休む時は許可をもらってください。
sentence_meaning: Please get permission when you want to take time off.

mnemonic: A bar 才 dropped across the gate 門 and that is the end of the matter. Books shut, everybody: とじる.
notes: 閉める しめる shuts a door or a shop. 閉じる closes something that folds, a book or your eyes.
sentence: 教科書を閉じてください。
sentence_meaning: Please close your textbooks.

meaning: to put on top of something, to pile up
mnemonic: One heavy 重 thing set on top of the last until the stack is taller than you are. Bags in that corner, please: かさねる.
sentence: 荷物はここに重ねてください。
sentence_meaning: Please pile up the luggage here.

mnemonic: Thread 糸 drawn out across a field 田 until there is hardly anything of it left to see. Her fingers go the same way: ほそい.
notes: 薄い うすい is thin as in not thick, a slice or a flavour. 細い is thin as in narrow, a thread or a finger.
sentence: 彼女は指が細いですね。
sentence_meaning: Her fingers are thin.
